title: Mars Fact Sheet
content: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System. It is known as the Red Planet because iron oxide on its surface gives it a reddish appearance. Mars has a thin atmosphere, mostly made of carbon dioxide. It has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos. The gravity on Mars is only 38% of Earth's gravity.

title: Jupiter Fact Sheet
content: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the Solar System. It is a gas giant with a mass more than two and a half times that of all the other planets in the Solar System combined, but slightly less than one-thousandth the mass of the Sun. Jupiter is primarily composed of hydrogen and helium. Its most famous feature is the Great Red Spot, a giant storm that is larger than Earth.

title: The Sun Fact Sheet
content: The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System. It is a nearly perfect sphere of hot plasma, heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion reactions in its core. The temperature at the surface of the Sun is about 5,500 degrees Celsius (10,000 degrees Fahrenheit). The Sun provides the energy needed to sustain life on Earth.

title: Earth Fact Sheet
content: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life. About 71% of Earth's surface is made up of the ocean, dwarfing Earth's polar ice, lakes, and rivers. The remaining 29% of Earth's surface refers to land, consisting of continents and islands. Earth has a powerful magnetic field caused by its rotating, liquid core.

title: Black Holes
content: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light or other electromagnetic waves, has enough energy to escape it. Black holes typically form when massive stars collapse at the end of their life cycles. The boundary around a black hole from which no light or other radiation can escape is called the event horizon.
